CVE-2026-116567.title: FreeSWITCH: Pre-authentication stack buffer overflow in mod_rtmp control-message handling
CVE-2026-116567.description: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.2, rtmp_handle_control() rendered an RTMP user-control message into a 200-byte stack buffer using an unbounded sprintf loop controlled by the wire message length. A body of roughly 70 bytes or more overflowed the stack before any RTMP login, because the handshake authenticates neither side. The flaw affects deployments that build and load mod_rtmp, which is disabled in the stock build and configuration but commonly exposes a listener on TCP port 1935 when enabled. One unauthenticated message can crash FreeSWITCH and end every active call; the constrained ASCII hex output has not yielded control-flow hijacking. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.2.

CVE-2026-123862.title: Node.js is vulnerable to a zlib denial of service via a stream destroy during a pending params() call
CVE-2026-123862.description: An uncatchable exception in the Node.js zlib streaming API lets a peer crash a process by disconnecting while data is being compressed. zlib.params() queues a flush and completes its work in that write's callback; if the stream is destroyed first, as pipeline() does when the peer goes away, Writable still invokes the callback with an error, but the callback ignores its arguments and asserts that the native handle still exists. The handle is gone, so an ERR_INTERNAL_ASSERTION is thrown from inside stream internals and bypasses the stream's error event, the params() callback, and the pipeline() callback, terminating the process. An application is affected only if it calls deflate.params() while streaming to a peer, which is uncommon. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

CVE-2026-88019.title: Apache Shiro: Saved form replay may weaken cookie security and expose form data
CVE-2026-88019.description:
When Apache Shiro is used with the Jakarta EE integration module, the automatic form saving feature weakens the security of a form that is resubmitted after login.
Cookies set by the application during the resubmission could lose their security attributes, such as `Secure` and `SameSite`.
In addition, the resubmitted form data and cookies could be sent to an untrusted host.
This issue affects Apache Shiro from 2.0.0-alpha through 3.0.1, only when using `shiro-jakarta-ee` integration module with form saving enabled (the default).

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which no longer replays the form over the network, and avoids this class of issues entirely.
Alternatively, you can set the `org.apache.shiro.form-resubmit-host` (String) and `org.apache.shiro.form-resubmit-port` (Integer) system properties to restrict the host and port that Shiro will connect to when resubmitting a form.

CVE-2026-99501.title: s390/pci: Fix MSI directed-mode teardown IRQ bit count
CVE-2026-99501.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/pci: Fix MSI directed-mode teardown IRQ bit count

On s390 with directed interrupts enabled, zpci_msi_teardown_directed()
frees the platform's maximum number of MSI bits (zdev->max_msi) instead
of the actual allocated count (zdev->msi_nr_irqs). This corrupts the
shared IRQ bitmap used by all PCI functions, causing lost interrupts and
heap corruption. Fix zpci_msi_teardown_directed() to only free the
actual allocated IRQ bit count.

virtio_blk: use synchronous quiesce in virtblk_freeze_priv()

blk_mq_run_work_fn() can call blk_mq_sched_dispatch_requests() through
blk_mq_run_dispatch_ops(). The dispatcher checks QUEUE_FLAG_QUIESCED
while the flag is clear. It can then be preempted before it gets a
request. At that time, it has no queue usage reference, so
blk_mq_freeze_queue() does not wait for it.

virtblk_freeze_priv() then calls blk_mq_quiesce_queue_nowait() and
blk_mq_unfreeze_queue(). A new request can enter the queue. The old
dispatcher can run again, use its old flag check, get the new request,
and call virtio_queue_rq(). At the same time, virtblk_freeze_priv() can
reset the device, delete the virtqueues, and free vblk->vqs. The old
dispatcher can then use a deleted virtqueue or a NULL vblk->vqs, and the
kernel can crash.

CVE-2026-99736.title: mm/shmem: fix accounting of swapin-error markers
CVE-2026-99736.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/shmem: fix accounting of swapin-error markers

A failed swap read replaces the swap entry with a swapin-error marker in
the page-cache and subtracts its pages from "alloced" and "swapped";
however, it leaves their block charge in place.

Removing the marker during truncate then subtracts from "swapped" again.
This can underflow the counters or make swapped reach zero while other
pages remain swapped out, causing swapoff to loop without finding them.

When installing the marker, subtract only from "swapped" and let
shmem_recalc_inode() reduce "alloced" and release the block charge.

Make shmem_free_swap() report successful removal separately from the
number of swap pages freed, so removing a swapin-error marker does not
subtract from "swapped" again.
